To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have discovered an impurity state in a high-temperature superconductor located inside the superconductive gap that is momentum confined and that vanishes above the critical temperature.

we have observed an in-gap impurity state that is confined in momentum-space near the Fermi-surface wave-vector positions, and that this state originates from weak impurity scattering between bands with different sign of the super-conducting-gap phase.
the impurity state is confined in the momentum space, and that it is located inside the superconductive gap of Ba0,6K0,4Fe2As,2.

the electronic structure of the Fe-based superconductors.
the physics of unconventional superconductivity, in particular with the interplay between magnetism and superconductivity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superconductivity in the Fe-based superconductors is not of the d-wave type, but is of the so-called s+ or s- type.
the superconductivity of the Fe pnictides is not of the conventional s-wave type, and that the pairing state is of the antiphase s+- type.
the superconductivity in iron pnictides and chalcogenides has a s$+$-wave symmetry with a change of sign of the gap between holelike and electronlike bands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have observed a signature of antiphase s$^+$ pairing in the iron-based superconductor Ba0.6 K0.4 Fe2As2.
the in-gap state observed in our experiment is a clear evidence for the antiphase s+ pairing symmetry in the Ba0.6 K0.4 Fe2 As2 system.
the superconductivity in the iron pnictides and chalcogenides is not a simple s-wave, but a mixture of s$+$ and s$-$, where the sign of the superconductor gap changes from one band to the other.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of disorder, the superconducting state is not fully homogeneous and that, in particular, the pairing state can be antiphase, i.e., the sign of the superconductive order parameter can change between neighboring Fermi surfaces.

, in the presence of weak scattering, the impurity state is confined in momentum to the vicinity of the Fermi wave vectors, and its spectral weight is strongly reduced by a factor of 10$^{−2}$ with respect to the normal-state impurity state.
the superconductivity of iron-based superconductors is not a conventional BCS-type superconductivity, but it is a superconductivity of an exotic kind.
